newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS - Poor Malaysian state sees bounty in petrochemical deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Poor Malaysian state sees bounty in petrochemical deal.

text.p: Malaysia's only opposition-ruled state of Kelantan launched a $800 million petrochemical project on Friday which officials said would be the key to reviving the economically-battered region.

Kelantan state-owned Keloil Sdn Bhd signed a deal with KUB Malaysia Bhd, a cooperative backed by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's government, to jointly build a petrochemical complex over the next five years.
The two parties exchanged documents, witnessed by Mahathir and Kelantan Chief Minister Nik Aziz Nik Mat, in an unprecedented show of unity in Malaysian politics.
"We may have political differences but we can do business together," Mahathir said in a speech at the signing ceremony.
Few details were immediately available on the project, to be developed on a 2,000-hectare (5,000-acre) site on the beach front of the state which runs along Malaysia's east coast.
But KUB Chairman Hassan Harun said it would trigger development in Kelantan, which lies on the northern border with Thailand and is one of Malaysia's poorest states.
"The oil and gas industry could be the catalyst for the development of Kelantan," Hassan told a news conference in Kota Baru, the state's capital.
"There's no other industry capable of pulling Kelantan out of its doldrums," Hassan, a Kelantan native, said.
Hassan said KUB was headed for a public listing on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange and could not disclose the contents of the project or its financial details.

"Our immediate task is to acquire around 5,000 acres of land from Kelantan landowners for the building of the plant over the next five years," Hassan told reporters. "Until then, we can't reveal further."

But Kelantan Chief Minister Nik Aziz, who heads the state's fundamentalist Parti Islam se-Malaysia (PAS), said in the latest issue of the party's newspaper, Harakah, that the project will cost two billion ringgit ($800 million).
It will be the "centre for downstream activities of the oil and gas industry in Kelantan", KUB said in a statement.
It added that equity will be jointly split between Keloil and KUB, and both parties will do a feasibility study to determine the total cost and initial capital requirements.
Officials said seven trillion cubic feet of gas was detected off Kelantan's coast two years ago by a consortium led by Malaysia's national oil and gas company Petronas.

"The exploitation of this was awarded to the JDA (Joint Development Authority) on oil and gas between Malaysia and Thailand. We want the next findings to be reserved for Kelantan," said a leading businessman in Kelantan.
Rivalry between Mahathir's government and Nik Aziz's PAS, which came to power in Kelantan in 1990, has thwarted development projects in the state until now, analysts said.
PAS has routinely condemned Mahathir, saying that while Malaysia's 12 other states have prospered under his administration, Kelantan has been largely ignored.
State officials said monthly household income in Kelantan was 1,081 ringgit in 1995, compared to the national average of 2,007 ringgit.

The state lacks the kind of high-technology industries found elsewhere in Malaysia. Its people depend basically on agriculture, fishing, textile-weaving and money remitted by their children working in other parts of the country and in neighbouring Singapore, Hassan said.
